newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs dampened by BOJ operation.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs dampened by BOJ operation.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were easier on Thursday following the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) move to leave a lower-than-expected surplus in the money market after the previous day's injection.
The BOJ drained 500 billion yen from the market in its regular morning operation, leaving a surplus of 70 billion yen, after Wednesday's surplus of 300 billion yen.
"The UC (unsecured call loan rate) popped back above 0.50 percent after their operation," said a dealer with a European futures house.
"I think they were a little heavy handed today. It would have been no sweat for them to drain 100 billion today and another 100 billion tomorrow," he said.
Dealers said comments by a key Finance Ministry official that market participants being overly pessimistic about the outlook for the Japanese economy also weighed on the market.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the International Finance Bureau, said recent economic indicators in Japan had been rather strong and said the market was taken up by "irrational negative exuberance".
December Euroyen stood at 99.07 at 1130 GMT after falling to a low of 99.06 against its IMM close at 99.09. June JGBs settled at 126.95 against their IMM close at 127.07.
Eurodollar futures ended flat as players awaited the release of the U.S. Producer Price Index and retail sales data for March on Friday.
September Eurodollars ended unchanged at 93.725 against their IMM close on light volume of 3,015 lots.
